procedure: Collect some items made of different materials, such as copper wire, nickel ring, glass bottle, paper clips, iron nail, eraser, wooden ruler and plastic comb.
Place the items on a table.
Bring the permanent magnet close to each item one by one.
Observe which items are attracted by the magnet and which are not.
Make a list of magnetic and non-magnetic materials.
aim: To identify magnetic and non-magnetic materials by testing them with a permanent magnet.

viva.question: What is a magnetic material?
viva.answer: A material that is attracted by a magnet.

viva.question: Is copper attracted by a magnet?
What is a non-magnetic material?
viva.answer: A material that is not attracted by a magnet.

viva.question: Is a paper clip usually magnetic?
viva.answer: Yes, paper clips are usually made of steel and are attracted by a magnet.

apparatus: Items made of different materials (for example, copper wire, nickel ring, glass bottle, paper clips, iron nail, eraser, wooden ruler and plastic comb)
diagram: Draw a tabletop with a permanent magnet being brought near assorted items; label the table, permanent magnet, iron nail, paper clip, copper wire, glass bottle, wooden ruler and plastic comb.
title: Identifying Magnetic and Non-magnetic Materials
precautions: Bring the magnet close to one item at a time.
Keep the items separated so they do not touch or attract one another.
Do not let the magnet strike or damage delicate items.
Keep the magnet away from electronic devices and magnetic cards.
result: The iron nail, nickel ring and paper clip are magnetic materials. The copper wire and glass bottle are non-magnetic materials.
